text:
infra-alerts-bot: Automated alert: rising ECC/Xid rate observed on rack-19. Started ~72h ago, current: 12 cards >20 ECC/hr, 3 cards >100 Xid. Kibana: https://kibana.internal/redwood/alerts/1934567890 :warning:

mike-ops: grabbing inventory now. quick note — serials trending from vendor lot 'A9-Q3-1125'. pattern looks like node-local cluster of failures, not network. :thinking_face:

tara-sre: any coincident firmware/driver pushes to rack-19 around Feb/Mar? could be software-induced regression.

sasha-ml: ran a bench reproduce on two suspect cards on bench lab. Steps: 1) cold start 2) 300W sustained 3) increase to 420W under mixed fp16+int8 load. ECC counts ramp up after ~45m. thermal cycling seems to trigger it.

jordan-eng: quick PromQL I used to pull the window: ```increase(nv_gpu_ecc_total{rack="rack-19"}[72h]) > 10``` also cross-referenced with `gpu_serial` label to map to inventory.

priya-eng-infra: immediate plan proposal: 1) cordon rack-19 nodes from scheduling 2) mark the 12 affected GPUs as drain candidates 3) run vendor micro-burnin on each card 4) if a card records >50 Xid in 24h -> RMA. Need procurement & vendor engagement.

alice-support: tagging the three dedicated customers with VMs on rack-19. Proposed maintenance window: 2026-03-18 03:00-06:00 UTC for drain+swap. customers get advance notice. :calendar:

procurement: vendor already flagged increased rework rate against lot A9-Q3-1125 in their internal logs. They asked for CSV of serials + build_date. Sending sample format: ```serial,build_date,model
SN-A91234,2025-11-18,RTX-A9
SN-A91235,2025-11-19,RTX-A9```

mike-ops: cost note — if vendor confirms a recall and covers shipping+replacement, internal cost ~0. If out-of-warranty or extended damage due to overheating, estimate ~ $24,000 for replacements + labor. We'll aim for vendor RMA first.

tara-sre: capacity impact: draining 12 GPUs reduces GPU pool in us-east-1 by ~9-12%. I'll open reroute rules to redirect batch jobs to us-west-2 and enable burst capacity for critical queues. Expect 10-20% increased latency on non-priority jobs during swap.

vendor-nv: (NVendor Support) We've opened TB-2026-07 for this symptom set (suspected solder bridging causing intermittent ECC/Xid increases under thermal cycling). Please open an RMA with serials and attach lab logs; we can ship replacement cards under warranty for affected lot. Also sending updated micro-burnin and an FW knob — optional but may reduce false positives.

mike-ops: owners assigned: priya -> vendor comms & RMA ticket, sasha -> lab repro + burn logs, tara -> scheduling/reroute & customer comms, procurement -> cost tracking. I'll create follow-up ticket in infra-triage and drop links here. :white_check_mark:

alice-support: filed the customer notice, set auto-escalation if any customer reports degraded performance during drain.

priya-eng-infra: sending serial list to vendor now, attaching time-series and bench logs. Will update thread when RMA ETA is in.

mike-ops: follow-ups: add a recurring probe to alert on serial-batch clustering (alerts should aggregate by vendor lot), add a telemetry tag for `vendor_lot` on inventory import, and add a postmortem doc linking bench data + vendor response. I'll start the PM doc template after RMA confirmation. :spiral_notepad:

sasha-ml: attaching brief repro notes in ticket: `thermal-swing.sh` stress harness + power sweep. If anyone needs the harness, ping me. :mag:
_meta: generated for dataset: unique rack-level solder-bridge batch RCA thread
